title: Salmon poke bowl
intro: Warm sushi rice, marinated salmon and crunchy vegetables in one bowl.

steps.t: Rinse the rice in cold water, stirring, until the water runs clear.
Put it in a pan with the water, bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Take off the heat and rest, covered. Then stir in vinegar, sugar and salt and let it cool to warm.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile, cut the salmon into 2 cm cubes, toss with soy sauce and sesame oil and chill in the fridge.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: In the meantime, boil the edamame in salted water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
steps.label: Edamame

steps.t: Slice the avocado and cucumber, cut the carrot into matchsticks and slice the spring onion.
Spoon the rice into bowls, arrange the vegetables and salmon in sections and sprinkle with sesame.

tips.t: Only use salmon sold for raw eating (previously frozen); it's the safe way to eat fish raw.
Swap the salmon for sushi-grade tuna or marinated tofu for a different bowl.

title: Squash and chickpea Buddha bowl
intro: Roasted squash and chickpeas, quinoa and kale with a creamy tahini sauce.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the squash, cut into 2 cm cubes and toss on a tray with 2 tbsp oil, paprika and salt.
Add the well-dried chickpeas and roast, turning halfway, until the squash is tender and golden at the edges.
steps.label: Oven

airfryer.t: Air-fry the squash and chickpeas at 190 °C for 20 minutes, shaking the basket twice, until golden.

steps.t: Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and simmer it, covered, in the salted water over low heat until it has absorbed it all.
steps.label: Quinoa

steps.t: Strip the kale from its stalks, shred it and massage for 1 minute with the remaining oil, salt and a few drops of lemon.
Whisk tahini, juice of half a lemon, cold water and a pinch of salt into a smooth, creamy sauce.
Divide quinoa, kale, squash and chickpeas between bowls, pour over the sauce and finish with pumpkin seeds.

tips.t: Pat the chickpeas really dry with a tea towel; it's the only way they crisp up in the oven.
Keep the sauce separate and the bowl lasts 2 days in the fridge, ideal for packed lunches.

title: Chicken burrito bowl
intro: Everything good about a burrito minus the tortilla: spiced chicken, lime rice, pico.

steps.t: Season the chicken with cumin, paprika, oregano, juice of half a lime, 1 tbsp oil and salt. Leave it to marinate.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it, covered, in the salted water on the lowest heat until absorbed.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Finely dice tomatoes and onion, add chopped cilantro, juice of half a lime and salt: that's your pico de gallo.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan with the remaining oil, turning, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
steps.label: Chicken

grill.t: Cook the chicken on a very hot grill pan, 6 minutes per side, until charred and cooked through with no pink inside.

steps.t: Meanwhile warm the beans and corn in a small pan with a pinch of cumin and salt.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Let the chicken rest, then cut it into strips.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Stir the remaining lime and some cilantro into the rice, then build the bowls with beans, corn, pico, chicken and sliced avocado.

tips.t: A pinch of chipotle or chilli powder in the marinade adds the right smoky heat.
Make it vegan: swap the chicken for sweet potato cubes roasted with the same spices.

title: Greek salad bowl with farro
intro: Greek salad turned into a full meal with farro: fresh, salty and summery.

steps.t: Cook the farro in plenty of boiling salted water until tender but still chewy.
steps.label: Farro

steps.t: Drain, rinse under cold water and spread it on a plate to cool.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Meanwhile, cut the tomatoes into wedges, the cucumber into half-moons, the pepper into strips and the onion into thin rings.
Whisk oil, vinegar, half the oregano, salt and pepper in a small bowl.
Toss the farro with half the dressing and divide it between bowls.
Add vegetables and olives, lay a whole slab of feta on top, pour over the rest of the dressing and sprinkle with oregano.

tips.t: For a gluten-free version use brown rice or quinoa instead of farro.
Soak the onion rings in cold water for 10 minutes: they lose their bite but stay crisp.

title: Vegetarian bibimbap
intro: Hot rice, vegetables sautéed one by one and a fried egg with gochujang sauce.

steps.t: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then cook it, covered, in the water on the lowest heat.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Turn off the heat and let the rice rest, covered, without lifting the lid.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile, blanch the spinach, squeeze it dry and season with a little minced garlic, sesame oil and salt.
steps.label: Spinach

steps.t: Blanch the bean sprouts, drain and season them the same way.
steps.label: Sprouts

steps.t: Cut carrot and courgette into matchsticks and slice the shiitake. Stir-fry each separately in a little oil; the shiitake with 1 tbsp soy.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Mix gochujang, sugar, vinegar, 1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tsp water to make the sauce.
Fry the eggs sunny side up until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Put rice in bowls, arrange the vegetables in groups, egg in the middle, sesame on top. Mix it all with the sauce at the table.

tips.t: Serve in a sizzling hot stone or cast-iron bowl with oil under the rice to get a crispy crust.
Add pan-fried tofu or kimchi for an even heartier bowl.

title: Italian rice salad
intro: The classic Italian summer picnic dish: firm rice, tuna, boiled eggs and pickles.

steps.t: Cook the rice in plenty of boiling salted water, keeping it firm to the bite.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Meanwhile, lower the eggs into boiling water and hard-boil them, then cool in cold water and peel.
steps.label: Boiled eggs

steps.t: Boil the peas in salted water, drain and let them cool.
steps.label: Peas

steps.t: Quarter the tomatoes, slice the olives and chop the giardiniera into small pieces. Flake the tuna.
Drain the rice, rinse under cold water to stop the cooking, drain well and toss with 1 tbsp oil.
Mix everything into the rice with the rest of the oil, torn basil, salt and pepper. Top with egg wedges.
Cover and chill so the flavours come together. Serve cool, not ice-cold.
steps.label: Fridge

tips.t: Keeps 2 days in the fridge: take it out 15 minutes early and add a drizzle of oil.
Many Italian grandmas add diced frankfurters or cubes of Emmental.

title: Oyakodon, chicken and egg rice bowl
intro: Chicken and egg, 'parent and child', simmered in sweet dashi and spooned over hot rice.

steps.t: Rinse the rice in cold water, rubbing it, until the water is almost clear, then soak it in the 400 ml water for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile cut the chicken into 3 cm pieces and the onion into thin half-moons. Beat the eggs lightly: the whites should stay streaky.
Bring the rice to a boil covered, then cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Turn off and rest 10 minutes without lifting the lid.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Meanwhile bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar to a boil in a wide pan. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the chicken and simmer for 7 minutes, turning, until cooked through with no pink left.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Pour two thirds of the eggs over the chicken in a spiral, cover and cook for 1 minute over medium heat.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Pour in the rest of the eggs, cover for 30 seconds and turn off: they should be set but still soft and glossy.
steps.label: Last eggs

steps.t: Fill bowls with rice, slide the chicken and eggs on top with their sauce and finish with spring onion.

tips.t: Barely beaten eggs, with white and yolk not fully mixed, give the classic marbled look.
Use mitsuba from a Japanese shop instead of spring onion for the authentic aroma.
If you prefer firmer eggs, keep them covered on low heat for 2 more minutes.
